Threat.value: When something takes longer than expected I assume something bad is happening
I jump or startle at ordinary sounds that would not bother most people
I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations

Memory.value: Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time
My memories of the event feel more real and vivid than memories of ordinary things
The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me

vignette: Kaihana had always been a man who thrived on routine and control. As an airline pilot, he took pride in his ability to navigate even the most turbulent skies with ease. But it was a different kind of turbulence that changed everything for him - a police encounter gone wrong. It started on a typical Monday evening, as Kaihana was driving home from a long haul flight. He had just dropped off his colleague at the airport parking lot when he noticed a police car following him. At first, he thought it was just a routine traffic stop, but things quickly escalated as multiple officers surrounded his vehicle, shouting and banging on the windows. The next few minutes were a blur of confusion and fear, but Kaihana remembered the feeling of being trapped and helpless as the officers searched his car without explanation. The experience left Kaihana shaken, but he tried to brush it off as an isolated incident. However, over the weeks that followed, he began to notice changes in himself. He would feel a wave of nausea whenever someone drove too close behind him or when he saw police cars on the road. Even ordinary sounds like car horns or sirens would startle him, making his heart racing and his palms sweaty. As time went on, Kaihana became increasingly convinced that something was always about to go terribly wrong. When flights were delayed or didn't depart on schedule, he would feel a growing sense of unease, as if the delay was somehow a sign of impending disaster. He started to avoid driving with colleagues or friends, preferring to take taxis or ride-shares instead. The thought of being in close proximity to others made him anxious, especially when he couldn't control the situation. Kaihana's memories of that fateful night remained vivid and terrifying. He would wake up in the middle of the night, reliving the fear and helplessness he felt as the police officers surrounded his car. The more he tried to shake off these memories, the more they seemed to haunt him. It was as if his mind was constantly replaying a horror movie that he couldn't turn off. The incident had also left Kaihana with a deep-seated distrust of strangers. He would feel threatened by people approaching him on the street or in public places, even when there was no apparent reason for concern. This hypervigilance made everyday interactions feel like potential landmines, waiting to be triggered. As a pilot, Kaihana's job required him to maintain a level head and focus under pressure. But with each passing day, he found himself struggling to concentrate on the task at hand. His fear of delays and his constant scanning for potential threats began to affect his performance in the cockpit. Colleagues noticed that he was more irritable and withdrawn than usual, but Kaihana couldn't explain what was wrong. The final straw came when Kaihana's airline scheduled him for a flight with a new copilot. The thought of being trapped in the cockpit with someone he didn't know or trust sent his anxiety spiraling out of control. He realized that he needed help to regain control over his life and his fears. Kaihana is now seeking therapy, hoping to learn how to manage his symptoms and rebuild his sense of security. As he sits in the therapist's office, he can't shake off the feeling that something bad is always lurking just beneath the surface, waiting to pounce. He knows it won't be easy, but he's determined to confront his demons head-on and reclaim his life from the grip of fear.
